title: Choose the look of KANDO
question: Nothing is built yet. Pick the direction you want for the entry screens, Home, Search and the provider page, or ask for a new hand.

options.label: Das Klingelschild
options.lineage: German enamel house-number plates and the doorbell panel of a Kiez building
options.thesis: Every helper is a nameplate by your door, and asking for help is ringing the bell.
options.viewport: A sun-yellow field, a big blue enamel headline, a doorbell panel of lit helper nameplates and one red bell button that says Hilfe finden.
options.risk: Heavy outlines and rivets turn childish or kitsch if the plates are not drawn with discipline.

raised.raise: A lit window on a nameplate means the helper is free today: the whole row of doors looks like houses with their lights on.
Total colour commitment: the whole surface is sun yellow with one enamel blue ink and one bell red, no neutral template underneath.

options.label: Die Samentüten
options.lineage: illustrated seed packets from a German garden shop
options.thesis: Each kind of help is a seed packet, and a booked job is something planted that grows.
options.viewport: A pale green morning, a big friendly headline, three tilted packets for Putzen, Garten and Hund, and one dark pill button.
options.risk: The garden and growth metaphor is the one most hopeful apps reach for, so it feels familiar.

options.label: Window-box shelf
options.lineage: toy-aisle window-box sets with gingham trim
options.thesis: Each helper is a boxed set with a lit window; lifting the lid opens their profile.
options.viewport: A shelf of two gingham boxes with windows onto each helper, a yellow 'free today' tag on the first.
options.case: Holds audience identification (warm, neighbourly, playful); loses clarity because it reads as a children's toy shop and trust needs a more grown-up plate.
options.risk: A toy shop look can undercut a product that handles money and ID documents.

options.label: Riso print
options.thesis: Blue and sun-yellow inks overprint, with one orange accent, on paper like a handmade neighbourhood flyer.
options.viewport: A loud blue headline with a warm orange offset, overlapping sun-yellow and orange blobs, pale yellow category cards.
options.case: Personal and hopeful, which fits; weaker on clarity for forms, prices and a payment, where overprint noise gets in the way.
options.risk: Misregistration reads as a flaw in a screen with money on it.

options.label: Wood-type manifesto
options.case: Loses both: it shouts, which is the opposite of inviting and trustworthy.
options.kept: Hard typographic hierarchy: one big slab statement per screen.

options.label: Teletext
options.case: Loses both: black and retro-technical is cold, not neighbourly.
options.kept: A strict grid with numbered pages gives every screen the same address.

options.label: Gravity rain garden
options.case: Loses both: an impossible world does not tell a household how to book a cleaner.
options.kept: One dominant motion idea per screen.

options.label: Origami crane
options.case: Loses both: calm and crafted, but a step-by-step folding diagram is a teaching tool, not a marketplace.
options.kept: Visible progress through steps, one active step marked with a gold dot.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean marketplace: white cards, a calm green accent, big photos of helpers, a search bar on top.
canonCard.viewport: A search field, a row of category chips and a list of helper cards with photo, rating and price.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other marketplace; the app already looks close to this today.
